question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in model-elected continuation subsystem with trusted cross-session delegate returns, or require a narrower RFC/API-security split first?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a small mechanical defect; it is a core product and security-boundary choice involving model-facing tools, persisted state, cross-session delivery, and plugin/SDK-adjacent trust rules.

options.title: Accept core continuation after proof
options.body: Approve the subsystem direction, then require a clean merge refresh and exact-head live proof for the security/session-state paths before merge.

options.title: Split API and runtime work
options.body: Land only a smaller reviewed API or internal seam first, then revisit cross-session delivery and compaction behavior in separate PRs.

options.title: Decline core inclusion for now
options.body: Keep continuation outside core or close this PR if the feature is too broad for the current core roadmap and risk budget.

recommendation.title: Accept core continuation after proof
recommendation.body: Approve the subsystem direction, then require a clean merge refresh and exact-head live proof for the security/session-state paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest observed history across the agent runtime, config, gateway protocol, and docs surfaces that need the product/security decision.
